prompts.text: What started as a one-time idea in your life but somehow became an annual tradition?
Tell me about a family custom whose origin nobody seems to remember.

A tradition becomes meaningful through repetition rather than how elaborate it was at the beginning.
Keeping one ritual unchanged for many years or letting it evolve with the people taking part?
Many traditions are really old practical solutions that people grew attached to.
Have you ever borrowed a tradition from another household because you liked the idea behind it?
A community wants a new tradition welcoming newcomers. What would make it inclusive and easy to join?
Describe a celebration that felt different after the people involved had changed.
What everyday action might future generations remember as one of our strange traditions?
What's an unusual fact you discovered accidentally and never quite forgot?

Tell me about a mistake that taught you more than the instructions did.
Curiosity often works better when you're free to follow a question nobody assigned you.
Learning a new skill through trial and error or watching someone experienced work through it slowly?
One question often creates three more when you realise how complicated something simple is.
When did you last look something up out of curiosity and get completely distracted by another topic?
You find an old tool with no label. How would you figure out what people used it for?
What's a lesson you learned outside school that has been unexpectedly valuable?
Is there something you understand better because you've had to explain it to somebody else?

Adventure can be a change in attention rather than a change in location.

Taking a new walking route to a familiar destination or visiting a place you've always driven past?
People sometimes know the attractions in distant cities better than the little landmarks near home.
If you could spend one day exploring an unfamiliar profession's workplace, where would you go?
A friend tells you there's something remarkable hidden in a regular residential street. What would convince you to look?
Describe a time when you left home expecting nothing memorable and came back with a story.
What's a familiar place you've been curious about but never actually entered?
What choice do you make so automatically that you'd struggle to explain why you prefer it?
The hardest decisions aren't always the ones with the most options.
You need to choose between two equally good opportunities, but neither has a clear advantage. What would help you decide?
Having a reliable decision-making rule or being comfortable changing your mind after new information?
Tell me about a time you realised you were following somebody else's preference without noticing.
Small defaults quietly shape people's days even when nobody considers them important decisions.
How do you decide which opinions are worth listening to when too many people offer advice?
Someone makes a decision you don't understand but seems content with it. What would you ask before judging?
What's a decision you once overthought that turned out to matter far less than you expected?
Have you ever deliberately chosen a slower or less convenient option because the experience felt better?
Do you remember past events more through pictures, conversations, places or something else?
You could safely revisit one ordinary afternoon from childhood for ten minutes. What detail would you try to notice?
Tell me about a memory you once considered unimportant that now means a lot to you.
People who shared the same experience can carry remarkably different memories of it.
Keeping a diary of tiny daily moments or taking one photograph at the same time each week?
The stories we tell repeatedly can become more polished than the original experience.
Have you ever compared a childhood memory with a relative's version and been surprised?
You find a photograph with no date or location. What clues would you use to work out when it was taken?
Describe something somebody else remembers about you that you have no recollection of doing.
What would you want a collection of your old messages to reveal about how you've changed?
What's something about everyday life that makes more sense after hearing how older people managed without it?
An older relative asks why people work from cafés. How would you explain the appeal?
Tell me about a story from another generation that changed how you saw an ordinary convenience.
A person can teach you a great deal about the past without giving a formal history lesson.
Learning a traditional practical skill from an older person or teaching them a digital shortcut they could use every day?
Generations often invent different solutions to the same basic problems.
What's a modern habit you suspect your younger relatives will find old-fashioned someday?
You can invite someone fifty years older than you to explain one part of their childhood. What subject would you choose?
Describe a surprising similarity you noticed between your experiences and those of someone much older.
How can people share advice across generations without assuming their experiences are identical?
What's an object you use every day but barely understand how it works?

prompts.text: How can you tell the difference between being physically tired and needing a change of activity?

Have you noticed changes in the birds, insects or trees around somewhere you've lived for years?
You find a seedling growing in a crack beside a pavement. What might have brought its seed there?
What's a moment outdoors that made you unexpectedly curious about something you could research later?
